dedupe_keys.name: analysis of critical infrastructure dependencies and interdependencies argonne anl gss 15 4 2015

description: This Argonne National Laboratory report defines critical infrastructure dependencies and interdependencies and sets out how to assess them. It covers characteristics of dependencies (upstream, internal and downstream), classes (physical, cyber, geographic and logical) and dimensions (operating environment, coupling and response behaviour, type of failure, infrastructure characteristics and state of operations), then proposes a multi-phase roadmap for nationwide assessments with data inputs, analysis activities and products for each phase. Frédéric Petit and eight Argonne co-authors wrote it as report ANL/GSS-15/4, published in June 2015; CISA lists it in its Marine Transportation System resilience resource matrix. Coverage is US practice but general in scope. Format and access: a free PDF through OSTI. Licence: US government report with no licence stated; free. Caveats: it is a framework without data, and CISA notes it is not port specific. Its taxonomy is widely used to structure cascading failure and resilience models. Related catalogue records are the UNDRR GAR 2019 interdependency paper by Lewis and Petit and the German inter 3 KRITIS interdependency guide.
